To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MIGS are the main cause of nonOhmic drain characteristics and the exponent x M is the measure of their influence on the transport.

the MIGS states control the transport in the drain characteristics of a carbon nanotube field effect transistor and the power law relation between the onset bias and the conductance is a result of the power law variation of the effective barrier height with gate voltage.

MIGS play an important role in determining the transport properties of metal/semiconductor contacts and the scaling behavior of the effective barrier height with the conductance is generic for metal/CNW contacts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of Schotky barrier formed at metal/1D semiconductor interface.
the electrical characterization of the transport in carbon nanotube field effect transistors (CNTFETs) in the OFF-state regime.
understanding the role of the localized states formed near the Schottky Barrier in the electrical transport of CNTFETS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MIGS is the main reason behind the power law variation of the onset bias with the zero bias conductance in the drain characteristics of a CNTFET.
the MIGS are not the only source of nonOhmic transport in CNTFET, but they play a major role in controlling the transport through CNTFET.
the role of MIGs in the electrical conduction of CNTFETS is very significant and needs to be considered in the device modeling and design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown a new mechanism for the electrical transport through the metal/1 D-semiconductor interface.
the MIGS play a significant role in the transport of CNTFETS and their role can be understood in terms of a microscopic model.
the transport through CNTFET is controlled by a power law relation between the onset bias and the zero-bias Ohmic conductance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MIGS are the key players for controlling the transport through the metal/CNT junctions and hence, for the performance of CNTFETS.
the role of MIG S in the transport is not limited to the ON-state only.
the MIGS are the key players to control the drain characteristics of the CNTFET.
